results.evidence: One trip report describes a single ~60-ft rappel off the summit block (oddly noting '55 feet of rope'); no second source gives the rappel length or the rope length needed. The row's own 30 m rope doubled reaches ~49 ft, so either the rope or the rappel figure is off, but no two sources settle which.

One trip report rates the dihedral ramp Class 4 and the summit slot Class 3-4; another peak-bagging report calls the finish an exposed class 3/4 scramble on the north side of the summit block; a third notes a class 4 step in the moat near the summit. The standard corkscrew therefore tops out at Class 3-4, not Class 2-3.

results.evidence: Sources split: one trip report rates the diagonal crack class 3+ or 4, while a peak-bagging report and a hiking trip report describe the exposed downclimb at the cairned corner as class 3. Neither 'Class 2-3' nor 'Class 3-4' is confirmed by two agreeing sources.

results.correct_value: Surprise Col (~6,900-6,920 ft) is the Clark-Johnson col, reached after crossing the moraine rim and Surprise Basin snowfields; the corkscrew starts there.
results.evidence: One trip report climbs from upper Royal Basin over the moraine rim and Surprise Basin snowfields to 6,920-ft Surprise Col, 600 ft below Clark's summit, and starts the route from there. Two other reports traverse Surprise Basin and aim for the ~6,900-ft notch between Johnson and Clark as the start of the corkscrew. The col is reached after the basin, so the waypoint order is right and the approach/itinerary sequence (col, then drop into the basin, then a second col) is wrong.
